page: Microsoft Azure E16as_v7 is a memory-optimized virtual machine belonging to the Easv7 family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features 16 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 8 physical AMD EPYC 9V45 cores with multithreading enabled. The processor operates at a clock speed of 4.5 GHz and includes 32 MB of L3 cache. This server is equipped with 128.0 GB of RAM, providing a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8.0 GB per core. It does not include local storage or bundled GPUs, though it is Premium Storage capable.

Benchmark results show top-tier single-core performance, with stress-ng single-core CPU and Geekbench single-core scores placing in the top 10%. Single-threaded gzip compression and bzip3 decompression also rank in the top tier. Multi-core performance, including stress-ng multi-core and Geekbench multi-core scores, falls within the average range. Memory performance is strong, as indicated by the PassMark memory score, though uncached large-block read and write memory bandwidths remain average.

The server exhibits a clear performance tradeoff: while single-core execution and text processing are exceptionally fast, multi-threaded scaling and large-scale workloads like 70B LLM inference are average to weak. This profile makes the E16as_v7 highly cost-efficient for memory-intensive applications that rely heavily on single-thread speed or moderate parallelization. Recommended workloads include relational databases, caching layers, text processing pipelines, and small-scale language model inference.
